name: Alt-lite
summary: A loose, mostly online and American right-wing current that emerged in 2016-2017 and is defined against both mainstream conservatism and the white-nationalist alt-right. Scholars and the ADL describe it as Trump-supporting, anti-political-correctness, anti-immigration (especially Muslim and illegal immigration), anti-feminist, committed to free speech and to the superiority of Western culture, while avoiding explicit white-identity politics. Critics dispute how sincere the distance from white nationalism is.
scope: The 2016-2018 American 'alt-lite' milieu as George Hawley (Making Sense of the Alt-Right; The Alt-Right: What Everyone Needs to Know) and the ADL ('From Alt Right to Alt Lite') describe it: right-wing figures and outlets (Milo Yiannopoulos, Gavin McInnes and the Proud Boys, Mike Cernovich, Paul Joseph Watson, Lauren Southern; Breitbart for a time) who share much of the alt-right's immigration and anti-political-correctness stance but stop short of white nationalism. The label was coined by the alt-right as a pejorative and almost none of those labelled use it for themselves. It excludes the white-nationalist alt-right proper, mainstream conservatism and the later splits of groups such as the Proud Boys.
